To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the activation enthalpy of a diffusion, creep, conduction, or sintering process is a function of the pre-exponent factor, and (2) the activation enthapy of the same process is a function the doping level.

The relationship between measured activation energy, h, and pre-exponential term, A 0, is a function of the doping and impurity level, and can be used to determine the type of disorder in the material, and to predict its behavior.

The relationships between the pre-exponential factors and the activation enthalpies, measured in the intrinsic-extrinsic region, are well defined and can be used to estimate the pre-exponential and activation enthalpy of a process in a given crystal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of ionic conductivity, and the determination of activation energies for conduction and diffusion.
the study of the kinetics of the diffusion of ions in solids, and the application of this to problems of the sintering of ceramics.
the relationship between the measured activation enthalpies and pre-exponential factors in the intrinsic and extrinsic regions for ionic crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relationship between the measured pre-exponential factor and activation enthalpy is dependent on the type of defect, and the degree of disorder in the ionic crystal, but is not related to the type of process being measured.

the relationship between the pre-exponential and the experimental activation energy for diffusion in ionic materials is not a linear one, but that the relationship can be linear over a certain range of values of h and that the range is dependent on the type of disorder present.
the compensation law and Meyer-Neldel rules are not general rules but apply to specific cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pre-exponential factors and activation enthalpies are related by the compensation law, but the relationship is not linear in the log A 0 - h plots.

, for the case of diffusion in ionic materials, the compensation law and Meyer-Neldel rules can be shown to be special cases of a more fundamental relationship, which is derived from the thermodynamics of the intrinsic and extrinsic regions of a material.
the compensation law for ionic crystals is a manifestation of the Meyer-Neldle rule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation enthalpy is not an independent parameter, but is dependent on the pre-exponential factors, which can vary by orders of magnitude.
the relationship between the pre-exponential factors and activation enthalpies for ionic conduction and diffusion is a consequence of the underlying physics of the process.
the compensation effect in ionic crystals is not due to the presence of impurities, but rather to the intrinsic-extrinsic nature of the material.
